g.text: Plain-language event triggers, evaluated over video clips
An operator describes an event in their own words. The service turns the description into an evaluation plan, runs the plan over each new clip, and stores a verdict with the frames that support it.
Operators review long stretches of video to find a few events. Rules written as code need an engineer for every change.
Operators need to describe an event in plain language and get a verdict per clip, with the frames that support it.
Accept a trigger written in plain language and show its evaluation plan before it runs.
Evaluate every new clip against each active trigger.
Store each verdict with its evidence frames and the plan version that produced it.
Let an operator replay a trigger over earlier clips.
Live stream analysis: the service works on finished clips.
Training or tuning a model per customer.
Create trigger: takes the description, returns the trigger and its plan.
Replay trigger: queues an evaluation over a range of stored clips.
List verdicts: filters by trigger, clip and capture time.
Clip arrival event: carries the clip location and capture time.
A model update can change how a description is read. Each verdict records the plan version, and a changed plan waits
for operator approval before it runs.
Decision: queue between API and worker
Evaluation runs asynchronously. The API returns once the plan is queued, so a slow clip never holds an operator
Trigger editor: description, generated plan, approve
Verdict review: clip, evidence frames, verdict
The numbered links follow one request from the console to a stored verdict.
